pronunciation_overrides.Tensorblue: tˈɛnsəɹblˌu (not in the misaki lexicon; accepted CTA)

lines.text: Ten thousand posts. Not ten thousand rows.
So where do new posts come from?
Lists built for this only create the rows on screen, plus spares.
A row that leaves the top isn't destroyed. It's reused for the next post.
In our test: a plain list, ten thousand rows. A recycling list, fourteen.
Android says it improves responsiveness and saves power.
A long feed is just a small loop of rows, refilled as you scroll.
